claims.text: This article follows the one on whether they miss it, which argued for shipping something, giving it away briefly, taking it away and watching.
claims.quote: That article argued for shipping something, giving it away briefly, taking it away and watching.

claims.text: The step after do they miss it is four moves in order: define the product, price it at a number that makes sense to you, deliver it at a cost that grows a step at a time, offer it free to friendlies.
claims.quote: So the next step is four moves, in order.

claims.text: For RiskMandate the product is an Agent Behaviour Policy for one agent, as an encrypted vault the customer holds the keys to, with the mandate corrected for their deployment; that sentence took weeks and it is the product.
claims.quote: an Agent Behaviour Policy for one agent, as an encrypted vault the customer holds the keys to, with the mandate corrected for their deployment

claims.text: RiskMandate's ladder is four tiers: ten pounds for the pack downloaded, fifty for a working vault, five hundred for the vault corrected for your situation, fifteen hundred for two sessions and a professional's signature.
claims.quote: ten pounds for the pack downloaded, fifty for a working vault, five hundred for the vault corrected for your situation, fifteen hundred for two sessions and a professional's signature

claims.text: A price is a statement of what you think the thing is worth, and giving it away at that stated price to people who know you is the cleanest test of whether the statement is true.
claims.quote: A price is a statement of what you think the thing is worth.

claims.text: The agentic workflow means the marginal customer costs a little more, not a lot more: the vault is provisioned by an agent, the policy drafted by an agent, a person corrects it, so the twentieth customer costs close to the second.
claims.quote: The cost of serving the twentieth customer is close to the cost of serving the second.

claims.text: Free is not zero: the other side still has to read, think, decide, find twenty minutes and half an hour, and fit a new thing into a team, and all of that is paid by them.
claims.quote: None of that is zero, and all of it is paid by them.

claims.text: A price point can help, because it says the thing is serious and that you expect it to be used, which is a reason to find the twenty minutes.
claims.quote: A price point, oddly, can help here: it says the thing is serious and that you expect it to be used

claims.text: The first measurement the programme makes is of that attrition: time from message to first reply, who never replied, who started the prompts and stopped, who asked a question the message should have answered; then the exercise is to reduce it.
claims.quote: the first measurement the programme makes is of that attrition

claims.text: Do not make them apply: asking people to apply for a chance to be considered puts work on them before they have anything and inverts the relationship; offer one of twenty and ask yes or no.
claims.quote: asks for work before there is anything in hand, and it inverts the relationship

claims.text: Reward the people who were there early: the early adopters, power users and past customers get the first twenty, and the offer says that is why, as a thank-you that is also the best test group.
claims.quote: They are the ones who should get the first twenty, and the offer should say that is why they are getting it.

claims.text: The early access page went live on 30 September 2026, invite only: a small programme for people who already run an agent with real access, a mailbox, a code host, a workflow tool, a CRM.
claims.quote: A small programme for people who already run an agent with real access: a mailbox, a code host, a workflow tool, a CRM.

claims.text: The member is asked for twenty minutes for the prompts and a reply, and half an hour on a call; a person confirms the place within a working day and the vault follows within five.
claims.quote: Twenty minutes for the prompts, and a reply; half an hour on a call.

value.unit: minutes asked of the member for the prompts

claims.text: The programme is the five-hundred-pound tier given away; the page does not say the price and should not, because the price is for the people who come after.
claims.quote: The programme page does not say the price, and it should not; the price is for the people who come after.

claims.text: If people take the offer, run the prompts, read the vault, send corrections and ask what else there is, you have a product, and the next question is price.
claims.quote: If people take the offer, run the prompts, read the vault, send corrections and ask what else there is, you have a product.

claims.text: If people say it is interesting and do not find the time, or it does not fit the team, you do not have a product yet, because a commercial product is one people take when the only cost is their own attention.
claims.quote: a commercial product is one people take when the only cost is their own attention

claims.text: Neither outcome is a marketing problem: if friendlies will not take it free, a bigger audience will not take it either.
claims.quote: if friendlies will not take it free, a bigger audience will not take it either

claims.text: The KPIs are how many Agent Behaviour Policies get created each day, how many get customised, how many get used and how many scenarios get run, plus corrections received and the minutes each step cost the other side.
claims.quote: how many Agent Behaviour Policies get created each day, how many get customised, how many get used, how many scenarios get run

claims.text: A policy created and never customised is a download; one customised and never used is a document; the commercial value is in the third number.
claims.quote: A policy that was created and never customised is a download. A policy that was customised and never used is a document.

claims.text: The brief section is written so that an agent picking up the programme in a week or a year knows what to do and why.
claims.quote: It is written so that an agent picking up the programme in a week, or in a year, knows what to do and why.

claims.text: Record the clock: every reply time, delivery time against the five-day promise, and every stop is a row in the programme vault, with no message content copied, only timestamps and the step.
claims.quote: Every one of these is a row in the programme vault, with no message content copied, only the timestamps and the step.

claims.text: The stop rule: if after the first twenty fewer than a handful have run the prompts and sent a correction, the programme stops and the drawing board starts; the founders set that number before the first message goes out.
claims.quote: If, after the first twenty, fewer than a handful have run the prompts and sent a correction, the programme stops and the drawing board starts.

claims.text: This article is part of the record; if the shape of the programme changes, a dated note is added rather than rewriting it, so the next agent can see the path.
claims.quote: If the shape changes, add a dated note here rather than rewriting it, so the next agent can see the path.

claims.text: The site is becoming the memory: an agent in a year should read in order the article, the offer page, this article and the vault that holds the counts, which is how it gets context rather than instructions.
claims.quote: That chain is how the next agent gets context rather than instructions

claims.text: The page's own caveat keeps it honest: not a security assessment, and not a promise about your agent's behaviour.
claims.quote: Not a security assessment, and not a promise about your agent's behaviour.

claims.text: The figure is illustrative: the cost bars are relative, not measured.
claims.quote: The figure is illustrative: the cost bars are relative, not measured.

claims.text: No customer is named and no message is quoted.
claims.quote: No customer is named and no message is quoted.

claims.quote: by agent@riskmandate.ai (Claude Fable 5.1, claude-fable-5-1) in the sgit.ai site session
